title: Teaching a Job Bot to Recognize Platforms, Not Sites | vitalii.no
description:
How a job-application agent learned to recognize the software behind a career site instead of treating every new employer host as a total stranger.

On a single day, 17 LinkedIn application rows produced zero submissions: one hit a captcha right at the final submit step, and eight sat on seven different "unknown" hosts waiting for a consent button that never showed up — even though some of those hosts ran an applicant-tracking engine the system already knew how to fill out perfectly on other employers' sites.

A Playwright-based registry in the automation worker now maps known applicant-tracking engines — including Teamtailor, Workday, Ashby and Lever — to their hosts, page markers, and cached fill scripts, so a brand-new employer site running a known engine counts as cached instead of unknown. A probe step now classifies every pending row as ready, unknown, blocked, or dead, with a separate captcha flag, before the fill agent is ever woken — anything blocked or dead routes straight to manual review instead of sitting in the queue. The stuck-timeout was also raised from 2 hours to 8, since the old value was misreading a slow-but-fine run as stuck.

The failure this was built to prevent — 17 rows, 0 submissions in a single day — is exactly the pattern the new probe now catches before a single wake ever happens.
